# MySQL on SQLite — vendored copy

`src/` is the `packages/mysql-on-sqlite/src` folder of [WordPress/sqlite-database-integration](https://github.com/WordPress/sqlite-database-integration) (GPL-2.0-or-later), version 3.1.3, commit `f05c1f9eecf13ff2f387c4be8acf1ae3befaa537`. Joomla 3.x UTD's SQLite database driver (`libraries/joomla/database/driver/mysqlonsqlite.php`) runs MySQL SQL through it.

It is unmodified except for the patches below, in `src/sqlite/class-wp-mysql-on-sqlite.php` (1–5, 7, 9) and `src/sqlite/class-wp-sqlite-information-schema-builder.php` (8), each marked "Joomla 3.x UTD patch". Reapply them when updating the package, unless upstream has fixed the same cases.

1. **`querySpecOption` / `selectOption`:** drop MySQL-only SELECT hints (`STRAIGHT_JOIN`, `SQL_NO_CACHE`, `SQL_CACHE`, `HIGH_PRIORITY`, ...), keeping `ALL` and `DISTINCT`. SQLite failed with a syntax error on them.
2. **`innerJoinType`:** translate `a STRAIGHT_JOIN b` (an inner join with a fixed join order) to `JOIN`.
3. **`sumExpr` → `translate_group_concat()`:** translate `GROUP_CONCAT([DISTINCT] expr[, expr...] [ORDER BY ...] [SEPARATOR str])` to SQLite's `GROUP_CONCAT(expr, separator [ORDER BY ...])`. Several expressions are concatenated; ORDER BY is kept from SQLite 3.44.0 on; with DISTINCT, a custom separator replaces the default "," afterwards (SQLite's DISTINCT aggregates take one argument).
4. **`queryTerm`:** a parenthesized query as an operand of UNION/EXCEPT/INTERSECT (`... UNION (SELECT ...)`), which SQLite rejects, becomes `SELECT * FROM (...)`.
5. **INSERT ... SELECT column names:** the SELECT's own column names were used to refer to its values, but unaliased values give duplicate names (several `0` or `''` columns, renamed by SQLite to e.g. `0:1234567890`), so `INSERT INTO t (a, b, c) SELECT 0, 0, '' FROM DUAL` failed with "no such column". Positional `columnN` names are used instead, like the package already does for VALUES.
6. *(Dropped with 3.1.1: upstream now translates date arithmetic itself, negating the value for subtraction, so negative intervals work; `DATE_SUB()` of a DATE also returns a DATE now.)*

7. **`RIGHT()`:** passed on as it is, but before SQLite 3.39.0 `RIGHT` is a join keyword only, so `RIGHT(` was a syntax error. Written as `"RIGHT"(...)`, a quoted identifier on every version, calling the driver's registered `RIGHT()`.
8. **Collations in the information schema** (still unfixed upstream in 3.1.3): `get_table_collation()` took the first `collationName` anywhere in a CREATE TABLE statement, often a column's (Joomla's `alias` columns are `utf8mb4_bin`), so the table was recorded with it; it now reads the table's own `DEFAULT COLLATE`, else its `DEFAULT CHARSET`'s default collation. Columns without a charset or collation of their own (`get_column_charset_and_collation()`, through `extract_column_data()`) take the table's, as in MySQL, instead of a hardcoded `utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci`, also when added or changed by ALTER TABLE (`get_recorded_table_collation()`). `BINARY` gives the table charset's `_bin`.
9. **SHOW CREATE TABLE** (`get_mysql_create_table_statement()`): writes `CHARACTER SET x COLLATE y` for columns whose collation isn't the table's, as MySQL does. Without it, a copy of a table on MySQL (`database:export`, `database:convert`) gave every column the table's collation.
10. **`translate_select_item()`:** a column in parentheses without an alias (`SELECT DISTINCT(t.alias)`, `SELECT ((title))`) is named after the column (`alias`, `title`), as in MySQL 8.4; SQLite named it after the text (`(t.alias)`), so code reading rows by the column's name found nothing (the Articles - Category module's Author Alias list). Expressions keep their text (`(title+1)`).

Sites whose database was created before patches 8 and 9 have the wrong collations recorded: `JDatabaseDriverMysqlonsqlite::repairCollations()` fixes them (run by the update script).

Known gaps on older SQLite (the package runs from 3.37.0; unused by Joomla core): `RIGHT JOIN`/`FULL JOIN` need SQLite 3.39.0, and `GROUP_CONCAT(... ORDER BY ...)` ignores the ORDER BY before 3.44.0.

Known gaps, not patched (unused by Joomla core): `DIV`, `TIMESTAMPDIFF(unit, ...)`, `LENGTH()` counts characters instead of bytes, `ADD COLUMN ... AFTER` adds the column at the end, `LAST_INSERT_ID()` after a multi-row INSERT gives the last ID instead of the first, `TRIM(BOTH|LEADING|TRAILING x FROM y)` is a syntax error, `SHA1()`, `REPEAT()`, `ASCII()` and `JSON_UNQUOTE()` don't exist, and `=`, `ORDER BY` and unique keys compare text with SQLite's `NOCASE` (ASCII letters only) rather than `utf8mb4_unicode_ci`: accents, full-width letters, `ß`/`ss`, non-ASCII case and trailing spaces make values differ which MySQL treats as equal. `LIKE` is the driver's own since 3.18 (below), as MySQL compares (non-ASCII case and accents ignored, a trailing escape character literal), also on `utf8mb4_bin` columns, where MySQL's would be case-sensitive.

Functions the package lacks or gets wrong (`IF()` until 3.1.0, which translates it to `CASE WHEN` itself, so the driver's is no longer called; Unicode `LOWER()`/`UPPER()`, `LIKE` (SQLite's `like()`), `FIND_IN_SET()`, `SUBSTRING_INDEX()`, `RIGHT()`, `LPAD()`/`RPAD()`, `UUID()`, `LAST_INSERT_ID()`, `CONCAT_WS()` (SQLite 3.44.0+ only), `SOUNDEX()` (only in SQLite built with it), and `REGEXP`, whose pattern ended at an escaped slash and printed PHP warnings for invalid patterns) are not patched here; the driver registers its own versions (`libraries/joomla/database/mysqlonsqlite/functions.php`).
